jobs.description:
**Job Summary and Responsibilities**  

As our **Program Manager of Infection Prevention,** you will help our facility’s patients, personnel, and visitors maintain a safe environment by coordinating all infection prevention and surveillance activities so they can benefit from a healthcare setting protected from the transmission of diseases and infections.


Every day you will assess, develop, and operationalize programs, policies, and procedures to address the infection prevention needs of the facility. You will be expected to conduct regular surveillance rounds, lead root cause analyses for healthcare\-associated infections, ensure compliance with federal, state, and CMS regulations, and provide expert consultation and education to clinical staff and hospital committees.


To be successful in this role you must possess strong analytical and communication skills, maintain current knowledge of infection prevention professional society guidelines, and hold a valid Certification in Infection Control (CIC). You must also demonstrate the ability to effectively manage multiple projects, work collaboratively with hospital administration and diverse staff, and provide data\-driven recommendations to support quality patient care.

* Responsible for the oversight of daily operations of the infection Prevention Department in regards to the facility compliance with Hospital Accreditation Standards, State and CMS regulations.
* Ongoing assessment and development of programs, policies and procedures, and forms to address the infection prevention needs of employees, volunteers, contract workers, independent contractors, physicians, registry workers and students in accordance with the guidelines established by the regulatory agencies.
* Works in collaboration with Hospital Administration to develop and manage an Infection Prevention Program that incorporates essential facility strategic plan elements that align with the goals, objectives, and risk assessments of the Infection Prevention Program.
* Develops and operationalizes the Infection Prevention Program’s annual risk assessment, annual plans, and annual evaluations. Identifies and implements updates to the Infection Prevention Program when new regulations and /or professional guidelines are published.
* Ensures all functions of the Infection Prevention Program are conducted including surveillance, rounds to inpatient and outpatient units including perioperative, procedural and ancillary departments, and mandatory reporting to local and state health departments, NHSN, CMS, etc.
* Maintains current knowledge of infection prevention professional society guidelines, best practices and regulatory requirements as demonstrated by attending infection prevention conferences and workshops, reviewing current infection prevention literature, guidelines and national standard and networking with Health System and external Infection Prevention Specialists.

**Job Requirements****Required*** Bachelor's degree in a healthcare related field and five (5\) years of experience OR Associates Degree in a healthcare related field and seven (7\) years of experience
* Three (3\) years of experience as an Infection Preventionist in an acute care facility
* Certified in Infection Control (CIC) within 24 months of hire

jobs.description:
**Case Manager I – Community Living Services**

**Full\-Time \| 40 Hours per Week \| Concord, California**

$1,000 Hiring Bonus

The hiring bonus is paid in installments:

* $500 after 60 days of employment
* $250 after 90 days of employment
* $250 after 180 days of employment

**Make a Meaningful Difference—With a Team That Supports You**

Adaptive Learning Center (ALC) is looking for a positive, dependable, and compassionate Case Manager who wants to make a genuine difference in the lives of adults with developmental disabilities.

This is an active, community\-based position—not a traditional desk\-centered case management role. You will work directly with a small caseload of adult members, helping them strengthen the skills, confidence, and connections needed to live as independently as possible.

At ALC, you will be part of a collaborative team that values communication, follow\-through, mutual support, and a shared commitment to the people we serve. We are looking for someone who brings positive energy to their work, takes pride in being dependable, and wants to grow with an organization known for its supportive culture and strong sense of community.

**Pay and Benefits**

ALC offers a generous compensation and benefits package that includes:

* 100% employer\-paid health and dental insurance
* Generous paid time off that increases with tenure
* 29 paid days off during your first year, including PTO and paid holidays
* 33\.5 paid days off annually during years two through four
* 38 paid days off annually beginning in year five
* $1\.50\-per\-hour differential for shifts worked on Saturdays and Sundays
* $1,000 hiring bonus

**What You Will Do**

As a Case Manager, you will support a caseload of approximately seven to nine adult members. Your responsibilities will include:

* Developing positive, respectful, and professional relationships with the members you support
* Teaching independent living skills, including household maintenance, organization, budgeting, and time management
* Assisting with meal planning, grocery shopping, and food preparation
* Supporting personal hygiene, healthy routines, and other daily living needs
* Monitoring and supporting medication routines when required
* Helping members strengthen social skills and build meaningful community connections
* Promoting personal wellness, home safety, self\-advocacy, and informed decision\-making
* Connecting members with community resources and opportunities
* Maintaining accurate documentation and communicating important information to the appropriate team members
* Collaborating with coworkers, families, service coordinators, and other members of each person’s support team
* Following through on assigned responsibilities and responding proactively when members need assistance

**Who Will Thrive in This Role**

You may be an excellent fit if you:

* Approach your work with patience, optimism, and respect
* Are dependable and understand that consistency matters to the people we serve
* Enjoy helping others reach personal goals and become more independent
* Communicate clearly, professionally, and compassionately
* Take initiative and use sound judgment when working independently
* Value collaboration and contribute positively to a team
* Are receptive to feedback and interested in learning and professional growth
* Can balance compassion with appropriate professional boundaries

**Qualifications**

* Experience supporting individuals with intellectual or developmental disabilities, autism, mental health needs, or learning disabilities is preferred
* Strong communication, organization, and interpersonal skills
* Ability to work independently while remaining connected and accountable to a collaborative team
* Availability to work at least one weekend day each week
* Valid California driver’s license and a clean driving record
* Ability to pass a Department of Justice background check
* Ability to complete a physical examination and TB testing
* Adult CPR and First Aid certification, or willingness to obtain certification after hire

**About Adaptive Learning Center**

Founded in 1988, Adaptive Learning Center is a nonprofit organization based in Concord, California. ALC provides integrated services that help adults with neurodevelopmental disabilities pursue greater independence, meaningful community involvement, employment, personal development, and an improved quality of life.

Our programs include Community Living Services, Community Connections social\-learning groups and activities, Vocational Support Services, Tailored Day Services, and Supported Living Services.

If you are looking for meaningful work, a strong and supportive team, and an organization where your dedication will be valued, we encourage you to apply.

Pay: $22\.00 \- $23\.50 per hour

Benefits:

The mission of Hope the Mission is to prevent, reduce and eliminate poverty, hunger, and homelessness by offering immediate assistance and long\-term solutions.

For participants living in interim housing, the path to that foundation requires skilled guidance, consistent support, and someone committed to making it happen. The Housing\-Focused Case Manager is that person.


Working under the supervision of the Program Manager, the Housing\-Focused Case Manager provides individualized, housing\-first case management to participants in Hope the Mission's interim housing programs. This role prioritizes rapid placement into permanent housing using low\-barrier, harm\-reduction, and trauma\-informed approaches — and is directly accountable for the documentation, engagement, and cross\-team collaboration that makes those placements possible.
